stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
The category of topological groups has limits and limits commute
with the forgetful functors to (a) the category of topological spaces and
(b) the category of groups.
conclusions:
The category of topological groups has limits and limits commute
with the forgetful functors to (a) the category of topological spaces and
(b) the category of groups.

reason: Products and equalizers of topological groups use the inherited product and subspace topologies, so both forgetful functors preserve limits.
A compact totally disconnected group has arbitrarily small open normal finite-index subgroups, and its inverse limit of finite discrete group quotients recovers the original topological group.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
The category of topological groups has colimits and colimits commute
with the forgetful functor to the category of groups.
conclusions:
The category of topological groups has colimits and colimits commute
with the forgetful functor to the category of groups.

reason: A solution-set and representability argument gives existence of topological group colimits, and the indiscrete-group right adjoint proves the underlying group-colimit property.

reason: Topological ring products and equalizers are computed in spaces and rings with induced topologies, proving existence and preservation of all limits.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $R$ be a topological ring. The category of topological modules over $R$
has limits and limits commute with the forgetful functors to
(a) the category of topological spaces and
(b) the category of $R$-modules.
conclusions:
The category of topological modules over $R$
has limits and limits commute with the forgetful functors to
(a) the category of topological spaces and
(b) the category of $R$-modules.

reason: Topological modules admit products and equalizers with the natural induced topologies, preserving limits in both spaces and R-modules.

conclusions:

reason: The topological-group colimit construction extends to R-modules, and the indiscrete-module right adjoint proves commutation with underlying module colimits.
